pois.text: The keys are still in it. Nobody took them. Nobody needed to.
pois.text2: In the glovebox: Nora’s drawing. A house with too many windows. I never showed her this place.

pois.text: WEND HILL — the letters cut deep. The stone around them has gone soft with moss.
pois.text2: Below the name, half polished away: tally strokes. Grouped in sevens. A lot of sevens.

pois.text: Fresh-dug. No stone, no name. Waiting.
pois.text2: Dry on top, damp an arm down. Dug slowly. Or kept ready.

pois.text: A stag — the crest from the invitation’s wax. One antler snapped clean off. Deliberate, by the cut.
pois.text2: The plinth names no family. Just: FOR THE HOUSE, FROM ITS WINNERS.

pois.text: Most of the names are weather-eaten. One date reads clear — older than this house admits to being.
pois.text2: Same mason’s hand on every legible stone. A century apart. The same hand.

pois.text: A chapel, locked long before I was born. The hinges say it intends to stay that way.
pois.text2: Scratches around the lock. Not from picking it. From under the door.

pois.text: Someone dressed the scarecrow in a dinner coat. The tailoring is better than mine.
pois.text2: There’s a watch chain under the coat. Gold. The watch is gone.

pois.text: Dry for years. Coins fused to the basin — wishes nobody ever collected.
pois.text2: All the coins are heads-down. Every one.

pois.text: Groundskeeper’s shed. The padlock is new. That bothers me more than the graves do.
pois.text2: Boot prints to the door. None coming back. Small boots.

pois.text: Coach doors. Wheel ruts under the moss — decades old and deep as trenches.
pois.text2: Chalked inside the frame, old as the moss: 41. 9. A third number, scratched out hard.

pois.text: The rope is gone. The bucket too. The dark down there has a smell.
pois.text2: I dropped a pebble. I waited. I’m choosing to believe it landed.

pois.text: This one fell face-down, and nobody turned it back over. Kinder not to read it, maybe.
pois.text2: Fine. I read it. The surname was mine. It’s a common name. It’s a common name.

pois.text: A child’s marker — smaller, whiter, newer than the rest. I stopped doing the arithmetic.
pois.text2: No dates. An epitaph, two words: COUNTED OUT.

beats.main: The gate was open. It shouldn\u2019t have been.
beats.sub: No lights on the road in. No cars. A house this size lit up like a birthday, and not one sound coming off it. I kept walking. I\u2019ve always been good at walking toward the wrong thing.

beats.main: Forty-one thousand, to men who don\u2019t take excuses.
beats.sub: Nine thousand more to the bank. There was a version of me that paid on time \u2014 Mara married that one. Now there\u2019s a stack of envelopes by the door I stopped opening in March.

beats.main: The rest \u2014 all of it \u2014 is for Nora.
beats.sub: Eight years old. A heart that skips a beat, then forgets to catch up. A man in Z\u00fcrich can fix it, for a number on his letterhead I can\u2019t say out loud without laughing. Or worse.

beats.main: It wasn\u2019t always me against the odds.
beats.sub: Mara kept the books. Kept me honest. Kept me. Four months from the word \u201cmalignant\u201d to the quiet \u2014 and in the quiet I found a table where the noise finally stopped. I called that peace. I was wrong about a lot that year.

beats.main: Two years, chasing one good night.
beats.sub: I lied to my brother. Lied to Nora\u2019s doctors about money that was always almost here. Tonight the lying stops. I leave with everything, or I don\u2019t leave. Either way it ends.

coldOpen: Three calls before sunrise. Men like that don\u2019t leave messages.
The hospital wants an answer by Friday. The only answer is money \u2014 the one thing I\u2019ve never learned how to keep.
Her side of the bed is still made. Two years, and I still sleep on top of the covers, like a guest.
Then it was there \u2014 slid under the door sometime before dawn. No stamp, no sender. Only a crest in red wax: a stag, one antler snapped.

THE HOUSE ON WEND HILL

Nine o'clock.

Take the old road. It will turn you.
Come as you are. Bring nothing.

— a friend

branchBeats.sub: Toward the stones. I told myself I was being thorough. I was being slow.

branchBeats.main: They buried people here. They still are.
branchBeats.sub: One hole open and waiting, and no name cut for it yet. I did the arithmetic I always do: how much, and who for.

branchBeats.main: The bell is right above me.
branchBeats.sub: Close enough to touch the door it hangs behind. It rang anyway. It did not care that I was here to hear it.

branchBeats.main: A path left, into the dark of the garden.
branchBeats.sub: Mara would have known what half of it used to be. She knew the names of things. I only ever learned the odds.
Then stopped, and nobody came after. There is a version of my house that looks like this in about a year.

branchBeats.main: The long way round the flank.
branchBeats.sub: Every step out here is a step I am not taking toward that door. I noticed. I kept doing it.

branchBeats.main: Coach doors, and chalk under the moss.
branchBeats.sub: Numbers. Forty-one. Nine. A third one scratched out so hard it tore the wood. Somebody else's arithmetic, or mine, written before I got here.
